India faces monsoon deficit, higher temperatures, and varied rainfall

India is projected to experience a monsoon deficit with higher temperatures due to a weakening monsoon in the second half of the season. While an El Niño poses a risk of below-normal rainfall, a positive Indian Ocean Dipole may offer some relief, particularly for southern India, potentially preventing a deficient monsoon phase. Some regions, like Surendrangar and Morbi, have already experienced heavy rain. Forecasts also indicate lightning risks and heavy rainfall in states including Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, and Punjab.
